To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have developed a new metastasis model in vivo; 2) we have demonstrated that the epithelial phenotype can spontaneously revert to a more mesenchymal phenotype; 3) we have shown that this transition can be mediated by miR-200 and miR-424.
We show that the metastatic process is associated with an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, which can be reversed in vivo, and that miR-424 plays an important role in this process.

1) we developed a metastatic prostate cancer cell line that spontaneously underwent epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), 2) the transition was mediated by a loss of miR424 and an increase in the expression of the miRNA family miR200, 3) the transition was reversible by ectopic expression of miR424.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new models of prostate cancer metastasis and their use for the identification of new therapeutic strategies.
the role of miRNAs in the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
the development of novel therapeutic agents that target the miR-424/miR-200 regulatory network in the treatment of prostate cancer metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the miR-424/miR-200 axis plays a role in MET in prostate cancer.
the metastatic selection in vivo of DU145 human prostate cancer cells resulted in a model of MET, and that this cellular plastic behavior is regulated by miR-200 and miR-424.
miR-424 is a tumor suppressor in prostate cancer and that its expression is downregulated during MET.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the miR-424/miR-200c axis regulates epithelial plasticity in prostate cancer.

the miR-424/miR-200 axis may be a key regulator of epithelial plastic in prostate cancer.
